question_text: A ball is thrown straight up with an initial speed of 20 m/s. Neglecting air resistance, how long does it take to reach its maximum height? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: At maximum height, v=0. Using v=v₀-gt, 0=20-10t, so t=2s.

question_text: A 2 kg object is pushed with a constant net force of 10 N. What is the magnitude of the object's acceleration?
explanation: Using Newton's 2nd law F=ma, a=F/m=10/2=5 m/s².

question_text: A block slides down a frictionless incline of height h from rest. At the bottom, it compresses a spring of spring constant k. What is the maximum compression x of the spring?
explanation: Energy conservation: mgh = ½kx², so x = √(2mgh/k).

question_text: Two carts of equal mass on a frictionless track collide. Cart A moving at 4 m/s hits stationary cart B in a perfectly inelastic collision. What is their combined speed after collision?
explanation: Conservation of momentum: m·4 = 2m·v, so v=2 m/s.

question_text: A car of mass 1000 kg goes around a circular track of radius 50 m at 20 m/s. What is the centripetal force required?
Three identical resistors of resistance R are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
explanation: For n equal resistors in parallel, Req = R/n = R/3.

question_text: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 0.2 m. What is the wave speed?
A torque of 20 N·m is applied to a wheel with moment of inertia 5 kg·m². What is the angular acceleration?
explanation: Using τ = Iα, α = τ/I = 20/5 = 4 rad/s².

question_text: A satellite orbits Earth at a constant speed in a circular orbit. What is the direction of its acceleration?
explanation: In uniform circular motion, acceleration (centripetal) points toward the center.

question_text: A mass-spring system oscillates with period T. If the mass is doubled, what happens to the period?
options: It increases by a factor of √2
explanation: T = 2π√(m/k). Doubling m makes T increase by √2.

question_text: A 0.5 kg ball is dropped from rest from a height of 2 m onto a hard floor. It rebounds to a height of 1.5 m. Calculate: (a) the impulse delivered to the ball by the floor, and (b) the average force if contact time is 0.01 s. (g = 10 m/s²)
correct_answer: (a) J = Δp ≈ 5.4 N·s upward; (b) F_avg = J/Δt = 540 N

question_text: A projectile is launched horizontally from a cliff at 15 m/s. If the cliff is 20 m high, how far from the base does it land? (g = 10 m/s², ignore air resistance)
explanation: Time to fall: t=√(2h/g)=√(2×20/10)=2s. Horizontal distance: x=v×t=15×2=30 m.

question_text: An object moves with velocity v = 3t² m/s. What is its acceleration at t = 2 s?
explanation: a = dv/dt = 6t. At t=2s: a = 12 m/s².

question_text: A 5 kg box is pulled by a horizontal force of 25 N. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2. What is the acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Friction f=μmg=0.2×5×10=10N. Net force F=25-10=15N. a=F/m=15/5=3 m/s².

question_text: A block of mass m is on a frictionless incline at angle 30°. What is its acceleration down the incline? (g = 10 m/s²)
A 2 kg object is moving at 6 m/s. How much work is needed to stop it?
explanation: Work = ΔKE = ½mv² = ½×2×36 = 36 J.

question_text: A force of 50 N is applied to push a box 3 m along the floor at an angle of 60° above the horizontal. How much work is done?
A 0.2 kg hockey puck moving at 10 m/s hits a stationary 0.3 kg puck in an elastic collision. What is the speed of the 0.2 kg puck after the collision?
explanation: For elastic collision with m2 at rest: v1' = (m1-m2)/(m1+m2)×v1 = (0.2-0.3)/(0.5)×10 = -2 m/s (reverse direction). Speed = 2 m/s.

question_text: An object of mass 0.5 kg moves in a circle of radius 2 m with a speed of 4 m/s. What is the centripetal acceleration?
explanation: ac = v²/r = 16/2 = 8 m/s².

question_text: A 1000 kg car rounds a curve of radius 50 m at 20 m/s on a level road. What is the minimum coefficient of friction needed? (g = 10 m/s²)
A resistor has a voltage of 12 V across it and a current of 0.5 A flows through it. What is the resistance?
A wheel starts from rest and accelerates at 2 rad/s². After 5 seconds, what is its angular velocity?
explanation: ω = αt = 2×5 = 10 rad/s.

question_text: A pendulum has a length of 1 m. What is its period? (g = 10 m/s², π²≈10)
A planet has mass M and radius R. The acceleration due to gravity at its surface is g. If the planet's radius doubles while keeping mass the same, what is the new surface gravity?
explanation: g = GM/R². If R doubles, g' = GM/(2R)² = GM/(4R²) = g/4.
